c5.title: C5 assessment
c5.note: Record evidence and uncertainty across the five C5 factors. Classification is a human assessment, separate from whether a claim is true or false.
c5.disinformation: Disinformation — deliberate intent supported by evidence
c5.contextHint: Social, political, security, economic and cultural setting; affected audiences.
c5.causesHint: Originators and possible motives. Distinguish documented facts from hypotheses.
c5.contentHint: The exact narrative, manipulated elements and intended audience.
c5.consequencesHint: Observed or potential effects on people and institutions. Label estimates clearly.
c5.amplificationHint: Channels, timeline, repeated posts and audience engagement. Similarity alone does not prove coordination.
c5.intentEvidenceHint: Explain what supports deliberate deception, or why intent remains unknown.
c5.sourcesHint: Cite evidence titles, original URLs, dates, contradictions and remaining verification work.
c5.conflict: Another editor changed this assessment. Reload before saving to avoid overwriting their work.
c5.intentRequired: Document the evidence of deliberate intent before selecting disinformation.

publicTools.title: Less noise. More time to investigate.
publicTools.mission: At Disbunk, our mission is to identify and counter disinformation quickly, through evidence and human review.
publicTools.challenge: Reviewing every claim or link one at a time takes significant effort. The internet is full of noise: repeated content and material unrelated to an investigation. Technology helps us organize that material so researchers can concentrate on verification.
publicTools.intro: HDBSCAN helps us find groups of similar claims, instead of asking researchers to discover every connection manually.
publicTools.example: For example, if dozens of claims recorded in Disbunk repeat the same narrative in different words, the analysis can suggest a group for researchers to investigate together. Similarity alone does not establish that posts are false or coordinated.
publicTools.groupingBody: We combine multilingual semantic representations with HDBSCAN to suggest groups within each team. Researchers examine the context and evidence, then decide whether a group belongs in a documented campaign.
publicTools.noiseBody: HDBSCAN does not force every claim into a group. Material without sufficient similarity stays outside the suggested groups. No claims are deleted, and every case remains available for review.
publicTools.earlierBody: Periodic analysis of recorded claims can help the team notice recurring patterns and topics sooner. Automated monitoring of news and social media is a future direction, not an active capability of this system.
publicTools.whyTitle: Why does this matter for Disbunk?
publicTools.whyBody: Our human resources are limited. The aim is for technology to handle part of the initial organization and reduce repetitive work. This gives the team more time to verify sources, assess potential harm and prepare evidence-based responses.
publicTools.boundaries: Every suggestion is reviewed by a researcher. Grouping helps prioritize investigations; findings depend on source verification and evidence.
publicTools.integrationsNote: We are expanding our research tools with translation, documentary sources and team communication.
publicTools.translationBody: Draft translation to support work across languages, preserving the original and human review. The feature has been prepared in Disbunk; service activation is still being configured.
publicTools.documentsBody: A planned integration for organizing documents and source material that support investigations. Documents and evidence remain part of a documented verification process.
publicTools.notificationsBody: Planned channels for team notifications through Slack, Discord or Telegram. Notifications inside Disbunk are active today; delivery to these external channels is not connected yet.
